notes: Corrected French typescript headed Théorème de Bertini et variantes.; no date, own page number or stated total count. Archive number 112 is retained as a comment. The page states theorem 1 on geometric irreducibility of a generic linear section with the written dimension bound; local statement 2 for unibranch, normal and smooth variants using the bad locus Z; corollary 3 on fundamental-group surjectivity with an inserted algebraically closed-field hypothesis; a numbered remark with competing 3/4 impressions; and the beginning of corollary 4, ending at si X. These are document claims, not verified theorems. The exact reservation is: On n'affirme pas, cependant, que (*) soit toujours surjectif (sans hypothèse de propreté sur X). This withholds an unrestricted surjectivity assertion; it does not say that the preceding proper-case assertion is unproved. Mathematical form prompted inspection of the slanted inequality, the cancelled formula opening, the X/Y source and the exclamation superscripts; no expected theorem or formula settled their ink. The slanted lower stroke of the bound is retained without changing its relation. Both pi superscripts in (**) are exclamation marks. The source X/Y, remark numeral 3/4 and d/x prose cell retain alternatives without a conjectured correction order. An opening parenthesis survives in the cancelled formula before (*). The grave è, unaccented Enoncé and non respé. remain literal. The raised local introduction is one insertion; the separate low underline belongs to cancelled Complément, whose colon remains doubtful. Supposons and the cancelled handwritten soit are readable. The first live soit stands before f, distinct from the cancelled soit after est. The field hypothesis is anchored after non respé. and before Alors. The live article contains an e/apostrophe mixed cell before cancelled inclusion. The transition slash and comma after reference 1 remain. Three displays and their two left-side starred labels are preserved using standard LaTeX placement commands. Four brown-toned rules and one brown-toned brace are drawn; no material or hand is inferred. Both verbal marginal notes have two lines; the upper first word is uncertain vrai, acronym E|S GA and numeral V|IV; the lower note reads vu. dans / EGA V, with the numeral doubt inherited. No external EGA/SGA publication history was consulted. The two unreadable cancelled words after Z→X remain approximate in count. All inventory elements are represented, including insertion guides, underlines and mixed cells. Equivalent H heading/emphasis and handwritten identity wrappers are not differences. All three readers initially received two unrelated scan-116 prior-note quotations due to the extraction error; they reported and disregarded them, opened no other page, and did not reopen images. The corrected extractor and input-scope incident record preserve this limitation. No OCR, external research, mathematical proof check or LaTeX compilation was performed.
